title: LELA: an LLM-based Entity Linking Approach with Zero-Shot Domain Adaptation
text: stands to gain. Through extensive experiments, we show that LELA systematically outperforms the true zero-shot methods, and even beats state-of-the-art classical and zero-shot approaches on multiple datasets. We attach our code for reviewing, which will be made available as an open-source library. Before the blossoming of machine learning and deep learning, many entity linking approaches (such as AIDA Hoffart et al. ( 2011 ) and SOFIE Suchanek et al. ( 2009 ) ) were training-free, but were bound to a given knowledge base. Today, methods that work on any input KB are usually embedding-based: BLINK Wu et al. ( 2020 ) , AcroBERT Chen et al. ( 2023 ) , ExtEnD Barba et al. ( 2022 ) , ReFinED Ayoola et al. ( 2022 ) , VERBALIZED Rücker and Akbik ( 2025 ) , the approaches in Févry et al. ( 2020 ); Yamada et al. ( 2022 ) , as well as the different zero-shot entity linking methods evaluated on the ZESHEL benchmark Logeswaran et al. ( 2019 ) : ReS Xu et al. ( 2023 ) , Uni-MPR and Bi-MPR Tang et al. ( 2021 ) , and E-repeat Yao et al. ( 2020 ) . GENRE De Cao et al. ( 2021a ) is a generative approach and mGENRE De Cao et al. ( 2022 ) is its multilingual extension.
